x: DeltaLoader lets you run native mods inside Stormworks: Build and Rescue. It consists of four parts that work together: Part What it is DeltaLauncher A Windows app. It lists mods from the DeltaV mods site, installs them, switches them on or off and starts the game. Injector (swinject.exe) Loads a mod DLL into the running game after checking that the game matches. The launcher installs and updates it for you. Version patch (swversion.dll) Built into the launcher. Shows the DeltaLoader label in the game; it is loaded before the mods. SDK Public C++ headers and sources for writing your own mods. Everything the loader knows about the game comes from a mapping: names, addresses, signatures and layouts observed from a legally purchased copy. The documentation says clearly what is proven and what is not. What you can do Install and update mods from a catalog with one click. Switch mods on and off, then start the game with exactly the mods you chose. Add your own meshes, textures, shaders and data to the game without editing the game folder (mod folders). Write mods in C++ that hook game functions, watch live objects, place tiles, change weather and more. What it does not do Single-player only DeltaLoader is for your own copy in single-player. It does not work in multiplayer, it does not bypass anti-cheat and it refuses to attach when an anti-cheat module is present. Do not load mods into other people's servers. It does not modify game files permanently. Overlays are restored when the game ends. It does not guess. If the game executable does not match the mapping, mods do not start at all. Where to go next Playing: start with [Installation](/getting-started/installation/), then [Installing mods](/players/installing-mods/). Making mods: read [Development environment setup](/developer/environment/) and [Creating your first mod](/developer/first-mod/). How it works inside: [Loader architecture](/technical/architecture/).

x: Is this safe for my save? A mod runs inside the game process, so a bug in a mod can crash the game. Back up your save before trying new mods. Does it work in multiplayer? No. DeltaLoader is for single-player. It aborts when it sees an anti-cheat module. Will it break when the game updates? Mods will stop loading until the loader is updated. That is intended: wrong addresses would corrupt the game instead. Does it modify my game files? Not permanently. Mods are kept in a separate mods folder, and the DLLs are injected into the running game. Mod asset files (meshes, shaders, islands) are shown to the game through an overlay or a virtual file system; with the overlay the files are laid over rom while the game runs and the originals are restored when it ends. Can I use Workshop addons and DeltaLoader mods together? Yes. Lua addons are the game's own supported route and run inside the game; DeltaLoader mods are native DLLs. They do not interfere. Are there mod profiles? Not in the current launcher. See [Mod profiles](/players/profiles/). Do I need an account? Not to browse or download mods. An account is needed to publish and manage projects. Where do I ask for help? On the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/HH3ezeD8BD). See also [Community links](/resources/community/) and the [GitHub repository](/resources/github/).

Load The injector checks the target: 64-bit, the right process name, no anti-cheat module, and the SHA-256 of the game executable. The DLL is loaded with LoadLibraryW. The game executable is not patched. The DllMain part of the framework starts your thread and checks the SHA-256 and all byte signatures in memory. If anything is off, sw_mod_start() is not called and the console says why. sw_mod_start() runs on its own thread. Until you set hooks, your code has no effect on game threads. Unload The loader (or the in-game mod menu) calls the export swmod_shutdown(). The framework sets sw::mod::running() to false, waits for your sw_mod_start() thread to end, calls sw_mod_stop() and removes all hooks of the mod. It waits until no game thread is still inside a callback of the DLL (sw::Hook::idle()). Only then is the DLL freed. If a callback is still busy after up to 5 seconds, the DLL is left loaded: a small leak beats a crash. Rules Loops check sw::mod::sleep(ms) or sw::mod::running(). Callbacks are short; slow work goes to the mod thread. Do not keep pointers into the DLL after sw_mod_stop().

A hook runs your callback when the game enters a function. The callback runs before the original code continues: void cb(void self, void user); // self = first argument (for a method: this) Ways to install a hook Call Hooks rt.hook_api("server.getTime", cb, user, err) A Lua API handler by name from the mapping rt.hook_ctor("c_scene_ropes", cb, user, err) The constructors of a class rt.hook_method("class", slot, cb, user, err) A virtual method by vtable slot rt.hook_rva(rva, cb, user, err) A known address (relative to the image base) rt is sw::mod::rt(). Each call returns a sw::HookStatus. Example #include "sw/mod.hpp" #include <atomic> SW_MOD("counter") static std::atomic<int> g_calls{0}; static void on_call(void, void) { ++g_calls; } void sw_mod_start() { std::string err; auto status = sw::mod::rt().hook_api("server.getTime", on_call, nullptr, err); if (status != sw::HookStatus::ok) { sw::mod::log("hook failed: %s (%s)", sw::to_string(status), err.c_str()); return; } while (sw::mod::sleep(5000)) sw::mod::log("calls: %d", g_calls.load()); } void sw_mod_stop() {} Status values Status Meaning ok The hook is installed. unsupported_arch Not x64. target_invalid The target is not inside the main module. already_hooked A hook is already at this place. decode_failed The first instructions cannot be decoded safely. relocation_failed A short jump or no memory in reach. alloc_failed, write_failed Memory could not be allocated or written. Limits Warning A callback reads integer arguments with sw::Hook::arg(n) but cannot change them. To change a value, find the caller and patch the constant it passes. Float arguments live in xmm registers and are not readable by arg. sw::Hook::install_replace can skip the original function. Hooks are removed automatically when your mod unloads; remove one early with unhook. Game events by name (for example the tile events) are in sw/events.hpp and sw/tiles.hpp.

All headers are in include/sw/ of the [public repository](https://github.com/DeltaV-Modding/DeltaLoader/tree/main/include/sw). The comments in a header say what is proven and what is not. Every call that talks to the game fails closed: it returns false or nullptr when the game does not match. Stormworks is a native program, and mods are native DLLs, not .NET assemblies. Loading is done with the Windows LoadLibraryW function by the injector. The DLL's entry point (DllMain, defined by SW_MOD) starts the mod thread and runs the checks. Unloading calls the export swmod_shutdown() and then frees the DLL, after all hooks are removed and no game thread is inside a callback. The launcher copies the DLL into the game's mods folder. A copy loaded by the injector is tracked (swinject mods lists the copies it loaded).

The runtime (sw::Runtime) is a singleton inside each mod DLL. It attaches to the main module of the game, checks it and offers: Address resolution from the mapping: Lua handlers by name, class vtables and constructors, RVAs. Hooks on function entries: the first instructions are decoded and relocated to a detour; the target must lie in the main module. Hook::plan runs the same decoding on arbitrary bytes without writing. Memory access with a readability check; writing is explicit. Object identification from the vtable pointer. Hook memory is allocated near the image so rip-relative displacements still fit. Callbacks run on the game thread that called the function. What is not done Arguments of a hooked function are read-only integer registers. Float arguments are not exposed.

Two independent checks run before any mod code starts: The injector compares the SHA-256 of the game executable on disk with the mapping. The mod's bridge compares the SHA-256 again inside the process and checks every byte signature of the mapping against the running code. If either check fails, sw_mod_start() is not called and the console names the reason. This is intentional: a wrong address would corrupt the game, while a refused start only costs you a wait. A patch that changes game code (for example the version label) checks the bytes at the patch site first and refuses on a mismatch.

Thing Versioned by Game The Steam build; the mapping is tied to the SHA-256 of one executable. Launcher Semantic version, published on the mods site. It updates itself. Injector Its own version, embedded in the launcher; older installed copies are replaced. Mods Versions uploaded to the mods site; the launcher compares and offers updates. After a game update, the mapping is moved to the new build by fingerprinting the machine code (addresses masked), then verified against the bytes. Anything that cannot be proven stays unresolved.

The smallest mod #include "sw/mod.hpp" SW_MOD("my_mod") void sw_mod_start() { sw::mod::log("started"); while (sw::mod::sleep(1000)) { // false as soon as the mod is unloaded // work once a second } } void sw_mod_stop() {} sw_mod_start() runs on its own thread. A loop must check sw::mod::sleep() or sw::mod::running(), otherwise unloading waits for it. 2. Hook a game function and count calls #include "sw/mod.hpp" #include <atomic> SW_MOD("counter") static std::atomic<int> g_calls{0}; static void on_call(void self, void user) { ++g_calls; } // keep it short void sw_mod_start() { std::string err; auto status = sw::mod::rt().hook_api("server.getTime", on_call, nullptr, err); if (status != sw::HookStatus::ok) { sw::mod::log("hook failed: %s (%s)", sw::to_string(status), err.c_str()); return; } while (sw::mod::sleep(5000)) sw::mod::log("calls: %d", g_calls.load()); } void sw_mod_stop() {} Other entry points: hook_ctor(class, ...), hook_method(class, slot, ...), hook_rva(rva, ...). A callback reads integer arguments with sw::Hook::arg(n) and cannot change them. Hooks are removed when the mod unloads. 3. Find living objects of a class std::string err; sw::Instances::track("c_scene_ropes", err); // once, in sw_mod_start for (auto obj : sw::Instances::list("c_scene_ropes")) { // later, any time sw::mod::log("rope object at %p", (void)obj); } 4. Weather and time #include "sw/mod.hpp" #include "sw/weather.hpp" SW_MOD("storm") void sw_mod_start() { if (!sw::weather::watch()) { sw::mod::log("weather: game does not match"); return; } while (!sw::weather::ready() && sw::mod::sleep(500)) {} // waits until the environment object was seen sw::weather::set_weather(0.8f, 0.9f, 0.7f); // fog, rain, wind (local only) sw::weather::TimeOfDay t; if (sw::weather::time_of_day(t)) sw::mod::log("it is %02d:%02d", t.hour, t.minute); while (sw::mod::sleep(1000)) {} } void sw_mod_stop() {} Note The writers change the local game state like the game's own handler; other players are not told. The sampler only uses the current values while the setting override_weather is on. 5.
